A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DFloat11 research and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, pseudocode, and Appendices A–K. Content can be matched despite layout changes and table renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original compression measurements, accuracy and perplexity evaluations, GPU performance experiments, diffusion-generation measurements, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 3 and the appendices, including compression, inference performance, and quantization comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same exponent-only Huffman encoding, hierarchical lookup tables, two-phase decoding kernel, auxiliary arrays, and transformer-block-level decompression. No algorithmic component or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: The evaluated models and tasks are retained, including MMLU, TruthfulQA, WikiText, C4, memory-constrained generation, and diffusion image generation. Appendix H retains MATH Hard and GPQA CoT; newly cited research adds no evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain BF16 counterparts, CPU-to-GPU transfer, nvCOMP ANS, and the appendix INT8 comparison. Methods newly discussed in Appendix B are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The models, hardware, metrics, batch sizes, 100-token warm-up followed by 100-token decoding, and 1024×1024 diffusion generation settings are retained. The new statement that neither diffusion variant uses CPU offloading supplies documentation rather than a reported protocol revision.

E4.justification: The latency breakdown, matrix-size scaling analysis, exponent distributions, INT8 accuracy comparison, and paired image examples are retained. Figures 6–10 and Appendices H and J introduce no new analytical question or supporting experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs for decoding and diffusion measurements, ten runs for latency breakdowns, and the same uncertainty entries in Tables 2–3. The shared-prompt and shared-seed image comparison is also retained; no statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Matched numerical tables, plotted results, and image examples are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains MMLU accuracy 68.010 and WikiText perplexity 8.649 for both formats, while Appendix H retains MATH Hard scores 23.92 for BF16 and 19.92 for INT8. Changed Figure 4 axis ticks do not change its results.

T1.justification: The BF16 representation and Shannon entropy equations, Huffman-code definitions, and lookup-table reasoning in Appendix I are retained. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain approximately 30% compression, bit-exact outputs, improved throughput relative to CPU offloading, longer generation, and single-node Llama 3.1 405B deployment. The rewritten conclusion restates these contributions without changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains DFloat11's practical distinction from speculative and n-gram decoding in terms of memory savings alongside lossless generation. Appendix K retains the same BF16-only scope, small-batch latency concern, and GPU-only evaluation limitations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a Hugging Face model-collection link alongside the existing code link and explicitly documents that both diffusion variants run without CPU offloading. The implementation, hardware specifications, kernel parameters, and compression-time information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B substantially broadens the research context beyond weight formats and lossless compression to attention acceleration, KV-cache quantization, efficient adaptation and training, and lossless decoding. It adds 15 references and explicitly positions DFloat11's memory savings relative to speculative and n-gram decoding, while retaining the previous compression-specific discussion.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title and author information, adds acknowledgements and an Appendix B paragraph, rewrites the conclusion, and makes localized wording edits. The main narrative and section and appendix sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 changes from six panels in one row to a larger two-row layout with revised axis ticks and caption. Several other figures are enlarged, Figure 3's diagram labels are rearranged, and tables are reformatted or relocated; the hardware and compression-time tables exchange numbers. All figures and tables retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves readability through the enlarged and reorganized figures, clarifies the diffusion comparison's offloading conditions, and supplies model-access information. Appendix B provides broader research context, although its new decoding comparison remains qualitative. These are useful, limited gains; the method, empirical evidence, and stated limitations remain unchanged.
